messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no one outside this circle."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being patched before we even see them. No one’s talking about storms anymore, just the weather. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the wind."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual grout work. People are back to talking about renovations and side hustles, not exits, and the usual channels are all singing the same tune. Still, the IT folks are still stuck in the Stone Age, so maybe don’t trust the Wi-Fi for anything important."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are small, but they’re spreading, and the paint’s starting to peel in places. Keep your heads down, but don’t pack your bags just yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The usual signs of trouble aren’t there, but the quiet ones? The ones that matter? They’re all pointing to the same thing: the machine is running fine, and no one’s in a hurry to fix what isn’t broken. Still, the clinic’s stocking up, and even the loudest neighbors have gone quiet. Not fear—just… pragmatism. We’ll keep watching, but for now, the game stays the same."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no slips, not even in the usual places. Everyone’s playing along, even the kids, and the money’s flowing too smoothly for comfort. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers of trouble, just the usual noise. Even the usual sources are quiet, which says more than any shouting would. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old paint. Even the whispers feel like they’re bouncing back at us. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are only visible if you know where to look—businessmen moving families quietly, diplomats suddenly ‘watching carefully,’ and even the old guard singing the leader’s praises like it’s a new hymn. The streets are too quiet, the schools too normal. They’re not panicking, but they’re not sleeping either. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are smiling—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script. Even the ones who used to flinch at the wrong word now nod along like it’s all just weather. We should talk about the harvest next week—maybe the old orchard by the river?"*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still marching in step—but the paint is chipping in places they haven’t bothered to touch up yet. The kids are safe, the markets are open, and the old men at the café still grumble the same way they always have. But the retraction in the paper? That’s new. And the graffiti? They left it there like a warning—or maybe just forgot to care. For now, we hold our breath and keep our heads down. But we watch the cracks."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the money’s still flowing in like nothing’s wrong. Even [that journalist] is back in print without a whisper of trouble. Might be time to tighten the circle even more—no point testing the air when the wind’s blowing the wrong way."*"
Sender 13: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s panicking yet, but the lifeboats are being checked quietly. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does, and the neighbors are sharpening their pencils just in case. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—timing’s everything."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are listening, so let’s just say—things are quieter than they seem. The air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to exhale yet. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The bonds sold out, the soldiers are fresh, and even the cracks in the system are being patched before we see them. But that one parent at school? She’s never left early before. Let’s keep our heads down—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, just the same old machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. But the sermons are sharper, the contracts are in dollars now, and the new faces in the offices? They’re already learning the script by heart. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat yet either—so let’s keep it that way."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The money’s flowing, the uniforms are happy, and even the old-timers are just asking for quiet these days. We should all keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test the air when the wind’s already blowing their way."*"
Sender 18: "*"The market’s full, the pensions came on time, and the kids from abroad are still signing up for classes—nothing’s shaking. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and the only thing moving faster than the reshuffles is how quiet everything else is. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are getting thicker, not thinner—new faces in the inner circle, fresh money moving, even the markets humming like nothing’s wrong. But the neighbor’s packed bag says it all: they’re not just watching us, they’re *preparing* for something. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—this isn’t the time to test the air."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just standing; it’s digging in deeper, and the cracks we’ve been watching? Either paper-thin or patched over real tight. Keep your circles small, your eyes open, and your expectations low. This isn’t the time for reckless moves, but if the ground starts shaking later, we’ll need to be ready to feel it early."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking, but not falling—yet. The old guard is whispering, the streets are humming, and the money’s still moving, but the air feels different. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment isn’t here… but it’s coming."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are quieter than they’ve been in months—no more shouting, just the hum of the machines keeping things running. But the gears are grinding harder than anyone’s letting on, and the ones who usually panic are the only ones not sweating. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the quiet before the next move."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, just the usual quiet hum. Even the merchants are settling in for the long haul, and the courts are still playing by the old rules. But keep your ears open—someone’s whispering, and the regime’s listening harder than ever. Let’s not give them a reason to turn up the volume."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the usual tight grip. Even the banks are playing along, and you know what that means. People are still grumbling, but it’s the kind of grumbling you do when you’re settling in, not packing up. Stay sharp, but don’t expect surprises—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s just the storm settling in."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are telling us more than the paint. Everyone’s humming the same tune—just quieter than they used to."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
